I have nothing on Toil & Trouble in the firm's stored knowledge, so I can't say what they want in case reports or how they sequence mediation and expert work. I won't guess at another party's practices. If you have a Toil & Trouble document or precedent, send it and I can compare it with Joad's requirements.

Joad's own instructions are on file, and they should drive the approach for C-2 whatever Toil & Trouble does.

**Reporting**
- Send a written report every six weeks. Confirm the format and length with Joad at the start, since the file doesn't specify them.
- Send a note within five business days after each deposition. Only one firm lawyer and one insurer lawyer may attend.
- Give immediate notice of any other JX-series spindle incidents.
- Send monthly invoice summaries to the insurer's claims handler, Perpetua Wallace, and copy her on anything bearing on coverage.
- Tell Joad the same day if the carrier reserves its rights, because Joad is watching its aggregate limit.
- Route all case communications through General Counsel Evander Thorsby. Refer media, regulator and customer inquiries to him, and make no public statements.

**Mediation and settlement**
- Assess the claim first, then send Joad an assessment and recommended range.
- Do not make or signal any offer above the already approved authority until written board sign-off is in hand. Verbal indications from directors or officers don't count.
- Joad needs about three weeks to prepare a board consent, so flag that lead time early and build it into the mediation date.
- Check with Thorsby before conveying any offer within the insurer's tier, since the insurer will want to be involved.

**Expert work**
- Consult Joad and get its approval before engaging any expert.
- Prepare several candidates per discipline, with credentials and prior testimony. Joad has offered to help identify candidates with standards-body experience, and it prefers design testimony to stay focused on the product at issue.
- Give Joad at least ten days' notice of any proposed product testing, and get quotes before commissioning it.
- Agree a written protocol before any inspection or testing. Both sides' engineers must be present, with no disassembly, cleaning or sectioning until agreed.
- Keep a tight circle around who sees test files.

**Sequencing implications**
- Protective order first. Joad won't stipulate to the authenticity of its test data or produce anything beyond what the court requires until an order with an outside-counsel-and-experts-only tier is signed.
- Expert approval comes before engagement, and testing notice and quotes come before testing.
- Start the board consent process early if mediation might need authority above the insurer's tier.
- Discuss any Joad witness with the firm and Thorsby before putting them forward. Don't contact Joad engineers or production staff directly.
